gadgets.payload: n/a (attempted: Object.prototype.shell = true together with Object.prototype.debuggingPort = "0 ; <cmd> ; #")
gadgets.effect: the argv injection half WORKS: ChromeLauncher.computeLaunchArguments destructures debuggingPort/executablePath/args/pipe off the options object, so a prototype value lands verbatim in `--remote-debugging-port=<value>` in the spawned argv, and @puppeteer/browsers spawns with a plain literal {detached, env, stdio}. The shell half does NOT: node 20.18.3 honours an OWN shell:true but ignores a prototype-inherited one, so the injected metacharacters stay a single argv element and never reach /bin/sh. Measured with a control (own shell:true shells out and prints uid=; inherited shell:true does not).
gadgets.trap: BrowserLauncher.launch() calls existsSync(launchArgs.executablePath) before spawning, which also kills the 'Object.prototype.executablePath = "/bin/sh -c ... #"' variant. Object.prototype.args is unreachable whenever the caller passes args explicitly (own property wins), so --disable-web-security cannot be added to an admin bot this way.
gadgets.proven_by: measured offline against the pinned packages (knowledge/chains/htb-intergalactic-bounty-recipient-array-differential-otp-mass-assign-needle-output-nunjucks-rce.json)
